headline: Gulf of Maine herring spawning closures begin in western Maine and Mass.-N.H. waters
dek: The seasonal restrictions bar directed Atlantic herring fishing in two inshore spawning areas through Nov. 3, with a limited incidental-catch allowance for other fisheries.
body: Seasonal spawning closures for Atlantic herring began Wednesday in the Western Maine and Massachusetts-New Hampshire areas of the inshore Gulf of Maine, the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission said.

The closures run from 12:01 a.m. Sept. 23 through 11:59 p.m. Nov. 3. The Massachusetts-New Hampshire area includes waters bounded by the Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Maine coasts, along with specified latitude and longitude lines used in the fishery management plan.

Vessels in the directed herring fishery cannot take, land or possess herring caught in either closed area during the restriction. Boats operating in other fisheries may keep up to 2,000 pounds of incidental herring per trip per day, and vessels transiting the areas must have fishing gear stowed.

The commission said insufficient biological samples were available to trigger its forecasting system, so the two areas moved to their default closure dates. Eastern Maine has a separate spawning closure that began Aug. 28 and is scheduled to run through Oct. 8.

Atlantic herring support marine food webs as a forage species and remain important to commercial and bait fisheries. The seasonal restrictions are intended to protect fish as they reach spawning condition.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Gulf of Maine herring spawning closures begin
seoDescription: Seasonal Atlantic herring spawning closures are now in effect in western Maine and Massachusetts-New Hampshire waters through Nov. 3.
